flagged.title: Short links carry no ASIN in the code
flagged.detail: Each submitted link is a /B0.../ short code that is not the ASIN. Product identity could only be established by following the redirect. All five were resolved by observation on 2026-11-20 and the observed destination is stored in its own field, separate from intended ASIN.
flagged.action: Resolved. Observed destination recorded per product; intended ASIN left null because none was supplied.

flagged.title: Submitted links carry no Associates tag of their own
flagged.detail: The submitted link.amazon URLs resolve to plain product pages. No tag parameter was observed on them, so they do not by themselves attribute a purchase to shopnow047c-20.
flagged.action: Every outbound link on this site is constructed as amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20 rather than reusing the submitted short link.

flagged.title: Compliance status of link.amazon short links is unresolved
flagged.detail: Whether link.amazon short links satisfy the requirement that a link not obscure the destination is not something we can settle from published policy text. Non-Amazon-owned shorteners are clearly addressed; this is Amazon's own domain. We are not claiming these links are invalid. The question is open.
flagged.action: Not depended upon. The site links directly to amazon.com product pages instead. Raised for review so the question gets a real answer from Associates support.

flagged.title: Tracking ID attribution unverified
flagged.detail: shopnow047c-20 is applied to every outbound link, but confirming that it is an active, enrolled Associates ID requires signing in to the Associates dashboard. That sign-in cannot be performed from here, and no first-party report was available.
flagged.action: Test one link per product in the enrolled workflow and confirm the destination and the tracking report before scaling. Until then, treat attribution as unconfirmed.

flagged.title: No prices shown
flagged.detail: Amazon requires price data to come from its API so it stays accurate, and prohibits price tracking on the site. No Creatives or PA-API credential exists for this project, so any price printed here would be a guess that goes stale.
flagged.action: Price fields are marked unverified and left blank. No revenue forecast or conversion score is presented.
flagged.sourceLabel: Participation Requirements §2(b) (prices via API only) and §6(y) (no price tracking)

flagged.title: No star ratings or review quotes
flagged.detail: Program Policies §6(t) forbids displaying customer reviews or star ratings unless they were obtained through Creatives API or PA API. Ratings were visible on the live listings but may not be reproduced here.
flagged.action: Rating and review-count rows are shown as withheld, with the reason. Not left blank, so nobody fills them in by hand later.

flagged.title: No product photography
flagged.detail: No licensed product images are available. Amazon Program Content may not be copied, stored, or hot-linked outside approved tooling, and stock photography of a different appliance would misrepresent the item.
flagged.action: Pages are deliberately typographic — colour, type and layout carry the design. The real fix is Creatives API access, which would supply compliant imagery.

flagged.title: Commission rates not asserted
flagged.detail: Category commission rates and fixed bounty amounts change and are published inside the Associates dashboard. We did not find a current public table we could verify at build time.
flagged.action: No earnings estimate, effective rate, or revenue projection appears anywhere. The commission-potential column in the product register is intentionally absent.

flagged.title: Search Console not verified
flagged.detail: The site is indexable and has a sitemap and feed, but no Search Console property has been verified because that requires account access we do not have.
flagged.action: A placeholder verification tag is present and clearly marked. Replace the token, then submit sitemap.xml. Until then, query data is unavailable and topic choice stays a hypothesis.

flagged.title: Reader capture has no backend
flagged.detail: The email capture form is present for layout and measurement but no email service provider is connected, so it cannot deliver a subscription.
flagged.action: The form is inert and says so where a reader would hit it. No address is transmitted or stored.
flagged.sourceLabel: Participation Requirements §3(e) (disclosing cookies, pixels, and other tracking)

flagged.title: Analytics endpoint not deployed
flagged.detail: A self-hosted collector exists in _worker/ and the client is written to POST five defined events. No endpoint is deployed, so the client is switched off rather than sending events into a void.
flagged.action: Deploy the worker, set SITE_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT, rebuild. Until then no analytics data exists and the dashboard says so. A zero-dependency reference collector now ships at scripts/analytics-server.mjs: same event set, same key allow-list, same scrubbing and 30-day retention as _worker/collector.js, so choosing a host no longer requires writing anything. To turn it on: run it (or the Worker), set site.analyticsEndpoint in data/products.json and governance.analytics.enabled to true, rebuild — the build holds the client inert if only one of the two is set.

flagged.title: Campaign ledger is empty by design
flagged.detail: There is no authorized first-party report yet. Every ledger row requires a timestamp, source, channel, eligible sessions, clicks and reported orders taken from an Associates report.
flagged.action: The ledger starts empty with its schema defined, so the first real report can be added without redesigning it. No placeholder numbers.

flagged.title: Content volume is below the Associates review bar
flagged.detail: Amazon's Associates Help, 'Application Review Process' (checked 2026-11-20, US help topic G8TW5AE9XL2VX9VM), says: "All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) – a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts." It also says: "Content on your website must be recent (generally within the last 60 days)." This site has 5 guides and 5 product pages. Amazon does not say whether product and hub pages count as posts, but 5 guides is below the rule of thumb on any reading. The account's own status and review history are unknown from here. Carried forward from the parallel-session register (arena-2ca62ce9, FLG-010), which found this first.
flagged.action: Do not submit or re-submit for review until the site has at least 10 posts and content dated within the last 60 days. The weekly cadence in the suggestions register (SUG-05) is the proposed path. Recorded as a commercial blocker, not a content-quality one.

flagged.title: Five analytics events were never defined in the request
flagged.detail: The brief referred to 'the five defined events' but never listed them, leaving the previous session to propose its own set. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-007).
flagged.action: Resolved in this build. Five events are now defined explicitly — page_view, outbound_click, guide_read, compare_view, capture_intent — and documented at /analytics/. The wording differs from the earlier session's proposal; the newer set is what the shipped client emits.

flagged.title: A self-hosted analytics endpoint cannot run on GitHub Pages
flagged.detail: GitHub Pages serves static files only, so a collector cannot be deployed there. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-008).
flagged.action: Resolved by design, not deployed. The collector lives in _worker/ as a dependency-free edge handler, deployable anywhere with a fetch signature. It remains undeployed — see FLG-011.

flagged.title: A prior build merged observed ASINs into the intended-ASIN field
flagged.detail: An earlier session on this repo (arena-6bd1be15) listed the observed redirect ASIN in a column headed 'Intended ASIN'. A redirect is evidence of where a link currently lands, not of what product was intended. The brief explicitly requires these be kept in separate fields. Found first by arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-016).
flagged.action: This build keeps intendedAsin null for all five rows and stores the observed destination in its own field. The register page shows both columns side by side so the distinction is visible rather than asserted.

flagged.title: Conflicting reports about whether Amazon was reachable
flagged.detail: The first session recorded Amazon.com as unreachable from the sandbox. Two later sessions, including this one, opened the live listing pages successfully with a fetch tool. Both are true: direct curl from the sandbox returns HTTP 000 for amazon.com, while the agent's page-fetch tool resolves it. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-017).
flagged.action: Recorded as an environment distinction rather than an error. All five listings were confirmed by page fetch on 2026-11-20. The earlier statement is superseded, not deleted.

flagged.title: Three independent site builds existed for this repo
flagged.detail: Two earlier sessions generated root-level sites on main (PR #1, PR #6) and a third (arena-2ca62ce9) built its own. GitHub Pages serves a single source folder, so only one site can occupy the root. This session built a fourth. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-018), whose register predicted exactly this collision.
flagged.action: Converged to one site. The earlier builds' complete data, toolchain and generated pages are preserved unchanged under archive/. Nothing was deleted and no finding was dropped.

flagged.title: Readers had no way to find the dashboard surfaces from the front page
flagged.detail: The brief required every dashboard surface to stay reachable while the front page led with products. Putting them in the primary navigation would have put the audit in front of the shopper.
flagged.action: Resolved structurally. The primary navigation carries five reader destinations only; all nine record and review surfaces are grouped in the footer under 'Record & review', so they remain one click from every page.

flagged.title: No seasonal content, because there is no seasonal demand data
flagged.detail: The brief asked for seasons and topic clusters. No seasonal query data was obtained from any source, so no seasonal calendar was invented. The five guides are editorial working titles, not popularity claims. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-015).
flagged.action: Clusters exist as two product categories. Seasons wait for Search Console query data — choosing December topics from instinct is the failure mode being avoided.

flagged.title: Author identity and brand name are still placeholders
flagged.detail: No author was named in the source material, so no byline was invented. 'Counter Space' is a working name chosen for this build and is not a registered brand. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-013).
flagged.action: Both need a decision from the owner. Before adopting the name publicly, check it is not an active trademark in this category. See SUG-06 and Q-20.

flagged.title: Cited register identifiers (S01, S02, S07, S24) do not exist in this repo
flagged.detail: The brief refers to S01, S02, S07, S24 and FLG-003 as though a source register already existed. It did not. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-014).
flagged.action: This build creates that register from scratch: numbered sources, ten policy checks with quoted clauses, and a per-row verification status. If the owner has a separate register, those identifiers still need mapping to it.

flagged.title: The word 'Sponsored' appears on two Amazon destination pages
flagged.detail: The destination pages for two products display 'Sponsored' near the product summary. It is unclear whether it labels the listing itself or a carousel item. Recorded as observed, not interpreted. Carried forward from arena-2ca62ce9 (FLG-006).
flagged.action: No claim is made about sponsorship status of any listing. Re-check on the live page before publishing anything that depends on it.

flagged.title: Tagged product links are live before the one-per-product Special Link test
flagged.detail: Product buy-boxes and the register link to amazon.com/dp/<observed ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20 for all five products. The per-product test required before scaling (FLG-003) has not been run; it needs Associates Central sign-in, which this build does not have. The site does not claim the submitted short links are invalid. The test is recorded as blocked on the Special Link test register. The counts are deliberately not written into this row: scripts/compliance-gate.mjs recomputes tagged links and test rows on every build and warns while the pair is unbalanced, so the register says *what is true* rather than what was true when someone last typed a number.
flagged.action: Owner runs one test per product in the enrolled Associates workflow and records the destination and tracking-report line in data/special_link_tests.json. Until then no further product link is added. If a test fails, the owner chooses the link method. scripts/compliance-gate.mjs fails the build if links go live while no open flag records the state — close it by data, not by silence.
flagged.sourceLabel: Participation Requirements §2(b) (Special Links use the Associates ID)

flagged.title: Placeholder site-verification token in every page head
flagged.detail: Every generated page carries <meta name="google-site-verification" content="REPLACE_WITH_REAL_TOKEN_FLG009">. The value is a placeholder, not a verification token. It is not a credential and it does nothing, but it is a visible defect in the published HTML.
flagged.action: Remove the tag from the layout in _src/build.mjs, or replace it with a real token from Search Console once the owner verifies the property (FLG-009). Not changed in this session; it belongs to the shared layout.

flagged.title: Every specification cited the Amazon listing, including values the listing does not state
flagged.detail: The source column on /products/ and /register/ linked every row to amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>, whether or not that page carried the value. Nine rows that had been recorded as 'unverified' are in fact published by the manufacturer, and three product pages had no manufacturer citation at all.
flagged.action: Fixed. Each row now resolves to its own source: Amazon listing rows still link to the listing; manufacturer rows link to the page that states them (chefman.com, emerileveryday.com, thermomaven.com, chefiq.com). The build throws if a row claims a manufacturer source without a URL.

flagged.title: The 8-quart Chefman's 450°F was presented as its maximum temperature
flagged.detail: The listing title says '450°F Hi-Fry Option'; the manufacturer states Hi-Fry 'raises the heat to 450°F for the last two minutes', against a normal range topping out at 400°F. This site had recorded 'Max temperature: 450°F (Hi-Fry)' and a guide called it 'the top of the range in this set'. That overstates a two-minute browning finish as a continuous capability.
flagged.action: Corrected. The row now reads '400°F standard range; 450°F Hi-Fry for the final 2 minutes of a cycle', and the basket-vs-oven guide describes it the same way.

flagged.title: Chefman's 8-quart family has at least five SKUs and the listing names none of them
flagged.detail: chefman.com publishes RJ38-8T-BLACK (matte black) for the 8-qt Hi-Fry machine; retailer records for this ASIN give RJ38-SQSS-8T and a stainless-steel body of 12.75 x 13.5 x 10 in at 12.8 lb. The two disagree on colour and model, so no dimension, weight or wattage from either page can be attached to this listing.
flagged.action: Left blank rather than guessed, and recorded on the product page. The figures are not in dispute; which SKU this listing ships is.
flagged.sourceLabel: Chefman 8 Qt Hi-Fry page (RJ38-8T-BLACK) vs the Amazon listing

flagged.title: Emeril's own page contradicts the Amazon listing on preset count
flagged.detail: emerileveryday.com states '25 Cooking Pre-sets' in its specification block and '10-in-1' in the product description; the Amazon listing states 24 one-touch presets. Three different numbers for one feature.
flagged.action: Recorded as 24 (the listing) with the manufacturer figure noted. Neither is published as settled. Unchanged from FLG-005's finding, now with the third number and its URL.

flagged.title: Navigation labels: parallel row SG-27 has no source document in this repository
flagged.detail: The brief names SG-27 as the navigation-labels row. Its source document was not provided, so no label set has been checked against it. The primary navigation carries five reader destinations, and the record and review surfaces are in the footer, as recorded in the design notes.
flagged.action: Provide the SG-27 document. Until then the labels stay as built and are not claimed to match SG-27.
flagged.sourceLabel: Board: cross-scope requests (SG rows not in repository)

flagged.title: RSS feed: parallel row SG-28 has no source document in this repository
flagged.detail: The build produces an RSS 2.0 feed at /feed.xml. The RSS 2.0 specification requires the channel title, link, and description, and uses RFC 822 dates for pubDate. Checked 2026-11-20 against the RSS 2.0 specification: the channel has the required title, link and description; each item has a title, link and description; pubDate uses the RFC 822 form; and the file parses as well-formed XML. That check does not replace SG-28's own requirements, which were not supplied.
flagged.action: Provide the SG-28 requirements. After deploy, check the feed in a feed reader.

flagged.title: Search Console: parallel row SG-29 is not done — no verification is recorded
flagged.detail: The brief names SG-29 as the Search Console row. No Search Console verification is recorded in this repository, and no sitemap submission is recorded. The build does generate a sitemap, which lists every page. Every page currently carries a placeholder verification meta tag, which is not a verification (see FLG-025).
flagged.action: Account owner: verify the site in Search Console, submit the sitemap, and replace the placeholder tag with the real token (FLG-025). This needs a Google account and is not something the build can do.
flagged.sourceLabel: Google Search Central, Build and submit a sitemap

flagged.title: Reader capture: parallel row SG-30 is recorded, but the form has no backend
flagged.detail: The brief names SG-30 as the reader-capture row. The capture form records a capture_intent event (EV-05) when submitted. No email service is connected, so no subscription is delivered (see FLG-010).
flagged.action: Owner decision: whether reader capture is wanted, and if so, which email service to connect. Until then the form stays inert.
flagged.sourceLabel: Flag register: FLG-010 and event EV-05

flagged.title: Policy and FTC quotes checked word for word against the official text (2026-11-20)
flagged.detail: Operating Agreement §5: the Associates statement and the 'misrepresent or embellish' sentence matched. Program Policies, Participation Requirements: §2(b) (price display), §6(a) (Program Content), §6(f) (keyword clause), §6(t) (ratings), §6(w) (link clarity), §6(y) (price tracking) and §3(e) (data disclosure) matched. FTC Disclosures 101: 'Place it so it's hard to miss', 'The disclosure should be placed with the endorsement message itself', and 'You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried' matched. The policy quotes in data/policy.json are the same text. POL-09 is an internal rule, not a quote.
flagged.action: Re-run this check when Amazon or the FTC updates a document (FLG-031).

flagged.title: Policy quotes are current only as of the document versions checked
flagged.detail: The Operating Agreement page shows 'Updated: October 15, 2025'. The Program Policies page shows 'Updated: April 14, 2026'. The quotes in this build match those versions. A later version can change a clause number or wording without this build knowing.
flagged.action: Before each publish and before any Associates application, re-check the quotes against the current pages.

flagged.title: All five submitted short links re-resolved on 2026-11-20; destinations unchanged
flagged.detail: Each link.amazon URL was opened again. CHEFMAN 6 Quart B04G1MEwY → B0CDY277D3; Emeril Lagasse 26QT B02NbDxp3 → B09B7SB46R; Chefman 8 Qt B00hJ57DV → B08DKYBTPH; ThermoMaven 1 Sec B0c8moW59 → B0DHZTCNR5; CHEF iQ Sense Gen3 B0f3GKalj → B0DZFD6R9Z. The product title on each landing page matches data/links.json. Prices and ratings seen on the pages were not recorded, as policy requires.
flagged.action: None. Repeat if a link is changed.
flagged.sourceLabel: Amazon listing (landing page of the first link)

flagged.title: The ASIN rationale in the brief could not be tied to an official Amazon definition
flagged.detail: The brief gives 'Amazon's ASIN definition' as the reason the intended-ASIN field is checkable. On 2026-11-20 no Amazon Help page giving that definition was found. The only Amazon-domain result was a Seller Central forum thread; its definition replies were written by sellers, not Amazon staff, so they are not cited as Amazon's definition. What can be checked directly is narrower: all five observed ASINs are 10 characters, A-Z and 0-9, and each observed destination ends in /dp/<ASIN> (data/links.json). This checks the URL format only. It does not show that a submitted link was intended for a particular ASIN, which is why the intended field stays blank.
flagged.action: Owner: decide whether the intended-ASIN field should be filled from the submitted link (FLG-019). If the rationale is kept, cite an Amazon Help page for the definition before publishing it.
flagged.sourceLabel: Seller Central forum thread (not Amazon Help; definition not confirmed as Amazon's)

ledger.provenanceNote: Each row must cite the dated first-party report it came from. Rows are added only from authorized Associates reports; nothing is estimated, modelled, or extrapolated.

events.name: page_view
events.fires: Once per page load, after the page is visible.
events.payload: path only — no query string, no referrer, no identifier
events.purpose: Which guides and products are read at all.

events.name: outbound_click
events.fires: On click of any element marked data-affiliate.
events.payload: asin, page path, position on page
events.purpose: The one number that matters most: which product earns the click, from which page.

events.name: guide_read
events.fires: When a guide reaches 75% scroll depth, once per page load.
events.purpose: Whether a question-shaped guide is actually read or just landed on.

events.name: compare_view
events.fires: On load of the comparison table page.
events.purpose: Whether readers want side-by-side or narrative.

events.name: capture_intent
events.fires: On submit attempt of the reader capture form.
events.purpose: Whether anyone wants a digest, before investing in an ESP.

analytics.reason: No collector endpoint deployed. Client is inert rather than silently failing.
principles: No cookies, no fingerprinting, no cross-site identifiers.
No personal data leaves the browser. The capture form never transmits an address.
Raw events are not retained beyond 30 days; only daily aggregates persist.
The counter is first-party and self-hosted, so no third-party processor receives reader behaviour.
